scales.eci_public: Epoch Capabilities Index, public, Bayesian fit of November 2026 (Claude 3.5 Sonnet = 130, GPT-5 = 150). Primary modelling scale.
scales.aeci_nov6: Anthropic ECI on the November 6 2026 fit (Fable 5.2 / Mythos 5.2 system card). Reporting scale, reached through the ECI->AECI mapping.
scales.aeci_own_card: AECI as it will be printed in the model's own system card: the Nov 6-scale value plus the scale drift expected over the card refits before then. This is the quantity that gets graded.

metadata.interval_convention: median with central 50%, 80% and 95% intervals (lo50/hi50, lo80/hi80, lo95/hi95); null where undefined
caveats: Small samples: 25 Claude models with a public ECI, 3 Fable releases, 4 Haiku releases, 13 models linking AECI to ECI, 7 AECI refit transitions.
Both indices are re-estimated on every update. Predictions on the ECI scale are in today's units; AECI own-card predictions include an empirical drift model built on seven refits.
AECI rests on first-party internal benchmarks that cannot be inspected; the mapping from public ECI may shift.
A frontier is a running maximum of selected, best-configuration results; record-setters are noisy winners.
Benchmark scores stop carrying information near their ceiling; the index scale itself is anchored on today's benchmark basket, so values far above ~200 have no direct empirical meaning.
Scenario weights for 2027-2030 are a documented prior, not an estimate. The sensitivity table shows how much the answer moves.
The model cannot see regime changes it has no data on (new architectures, export controls, a compute shock, a pause).
Release dates come from the site's release forecaster; its errors pass straight through.

trend.note: Record-setting releases since Claude 3 Opus (March 2024). 'hinge' = piecewise linear with unknown changepoint; 'jump' = constant slope with a one-time level shift. BIC weights compare the four forms on the published point estimates; the slope-ratio interval is from the bootstrap over models and Epoch posterior draws.

families.note: Offsets are ECI minus the piecewise reference line through Anthropic's record-setters, weighted toward recent releases (half-life 1.5 years). 'pooled' is the empirical-Bayes estimate used by the 'mean' predictor; 'last' is the family's most recent offset, used by the 'last' predictor.
families.mythos: Mythos is the restricted twin of Fable (same underlying model per Anthropic). Public ECI scores Fable only, so on the ECI scale Mythos uses Fable's history; AECI is printed for Mythos only.

aeci.primary_scale: Public ECI is the modelling scale: 256 models from all labs over four years, published posterior draws, and benchmark-level inputs that let the scale be refitted. AECI has 14 released models on one fit, is built on first-party internal benchmarks and is re-estimated by every card. AECI is the headline *reporting* scale: every prediction is carried to it through the mapping below.
aeci.divergence_note: Below public ECI ~157 (through Opus 4.6) the two scales agree within about 1 point. For every model released since June 2026 AECI is 3.7-6.2 points higher. A one-time level shift fits that better than a steadily widening gap, but five points cannot separate the two, so both forms are carried.

drift.note: Per-refit change in printed AECI of frontier models between consecutive card fits. Seven transitions: five near zero, two near +5 (the Sept 18 fit and the Haiku 5.5 card fit).

leave_one_out.caveat: n=7 transitions; coverage figures are indicative only

Everything here is extrapolation; values are capped at 100000 hours (about 50 work-years), beyond which the number has no operational meaning.

scenarios.definition: Compute/supply-limited: training-compute growth falls on the 'low' driver path (2.5x, 2x, 1.5x, 1.5x per year 2027-30) and algorithmic progress falls back to 0.6-1.0x its pre-break rate within a year.
One-time jump: the 2025-26 step up was a level shift. Pace returns within six months to 1.0-1.4x the pre-break slope (at 5x/yr compute), then follows the 'central' compute path down.
New trend holds: algorithmic progress stays at the multiplier implied by the post-break slope; compute follows the 'central' driver path (5x, 4x, 3x, 2.5x).

AI R&D feedback: the algorithmic multiplier doubles every 6-12 months until it reaches 4-7.5x (total pace ~3-5x pre-break, as in research note 3), then stays there; 60-100% of the excess over 'hold' is realised; compute on the 'central' or 'high' path.
Bounded explosive tail: the multiplier doubles every 3-6 months to a peak of 8-30x (Forethought's 'won't be 30X' cap), holds 1-2 years, then settles at 3-6x; same 60-100% realisation haircut.

frontier.design: Monthly origins; target = running-max public ECI held at origin + h. Candidates are refitted on models released before each origin (bootstrap B=20). 'stacked' uses weights learned only from folds whose target date precedes the origin (equal weights until 10 such folds exist).

release.design: Folds are (Claude release, lead) for leads of 0, 3 and 6 months. The origin is the release date minus the lead; everything is refitted on models released strictly before the origin; the model is given the release's actual date and version type. A fold exists only if the release is the next one in its family as seen from the origin, which is why few folds exist at 3 and 6 months (families ship every ~3 months). Lead 0 is a day-of nowcast. Baseline intervals are a normal centred on the baseline with the sd of its own earlier errors at that lead (from its 5th fold). Tables use the folds on which every baseline exists.
release.combination_note: The four combination rules and the seven single candidates score within noise of each other on release folds (the lead is short, so the candidates barely differ at the target date). The frontier folds, with longer horizons, favour the pooled candidate. The live forecast therefore uses the 'blend' rule: the average of the frontier-fold stacking weights, the release-fold stacking weights and equal weights.

calibration.rule: Per level, the larger of the lead-0 and lead>0 factors; never below 1.

version_type_effect.rule: switched on only if it lowers CRPS by 2% or more

bias_correction_test.note: The model under-predicted on average (positive bias). Subtracting the rolling mean of earlier errors did not reduce out-of-sample error, so no correction is applied.

benchmarks.design: Same folds as the release backtest. Each benchmark's link is refitted on models released before the origin (and must pass the inclusion rule at that date); the release's score is predicted from (a) its predicted ability ('model') and (b) its true ability ('link_given_true_ability', isolating link error). Baseline: the previous model in the family on the same benchmark.
benchmarks.research_note_reference: held-out RMSE 0.092, MAE 0.067 with ability known (research note 1)

irt_refit_check.design: Own least-squares 2PL refit of Epoch's benchmark-level inputs. For every fold origin, the IRT is refitted on models released on or before that date only and mapped to ECI units by a monotone alignment to the published ECI of those same models; the release backtest is rerun with history from the origin's vintage and the target's 'actual' from the release date's vintage.
irt_refit_check.caveat: Scores in Epoch's input file are today's collection; a score measured after the origin for a model released before it cannot be removed (no timestamps).

aeci_drift_leave_one_out.caveat: n=7 transitions; coverage figures are indicative only

ability.rule: Per level, the larger of the lead-0 and lead>0 factors; never below 1.

calibration.method: Conformal-style: per nominal level, the factor by which the interval must be stretched about the median to cover the stated share of backtest outcomes; learned on earlier folds only when scoring (rolling), and on all folds for the live forecast; floored at 1.

reference_class.note: Quarterly origins on record series; slopes over (t0-3,t0-1], (t0-1,t0], (t0,t0+1]. Nearly all rows are the same 2024 episode seen through overlapping windows.
